sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: through this sum alone, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 38% to about 1%, being a woman to about 2%, typical angina to about 5%, non-anginal chest pain to about 9%, atypical angina to about 15% and chest pain on exercise to about 34%; all of these also act through the parts below.

parts.original_hypothesis: Additive composition at the logit, then sigmoid: logit = -1.258 + 15 direct input terms (SD 3.19; largest ca +1.37, sex:0 -1.62, fbs:0 +1.29, chol +0.63, cp:4 +0.61, slope:1 -0.61) + 1.470*ischaemia_gate(557) + 1.964*risk_factor_gate(1239) - 1.275*thalach_protective_gate(2124) - 0.463*thal_fixed_defect_chain(3860) + 0.193*no_exang_unit(6805) - 0.244*cp3_nonanginal_unit(7140). Hidden part SD 2.84; the ischaemia hub and risk-factor gate carry almost all of it. Inputs sex:1, cp:2, restecg:1, thal:3 have no edges (zero effect). Evidence (train): Train n=242: AUC 0.9589, acc 0.901. Logit = -1.258 + direct terms (SD 3.19) + hidden terms (SD 2.84): 1.470*557 (SD 1.75), 1.964*1239 (SD 1.50), -1.275*2124 (SD 0.46), -0.244*7140 (SD 0.16), 0.193*6805 (SD 0.07), -0.463*3860 (SD 0.025). Counterfactual flips (mean / range of logit change): female -1.72 [-3.14, +0.45]; exercise angina +0.85 [-0.32, +2.23]; diabetes +0.08 [-3.62, +7.19] - diabetes is protective on its own (direct fbs:0 edge, the known Cleveland quirk) but strongly risk-raising when combined with angina, ischaemia or female sex via 1239 and 557. parts.name: ischaemia_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Serial composition: 557 = ReLU(-0.612 + 1.585 oldpeak + 0.699 slope:2 + 0.543 thal:7 - 0.954 slope:3 - 0.559 fbs:0 + 0.048*8140 - 1.255*slope3_lowbp_veto), with 8140 = 2.242 + 0.996 restecg:2 an always-on affine relay (adds 0.06 or 0.16). It is a one-sided ischaemia score (ST depression, flat slope, reversible thal defect, high fasting sugar) that the low-BP/downsloping veto 2961 switches off. It is the hub of the network: read out +1.470 directly and also feeds the risk-factor gate 1239 and its second hinge 9147. Evidence (train): Train n=242: 557 on in 84/242 rows (35%); y=0.80 when on vs 0.25 off. By thal: on in 12% of normal-thal rows, 66% of reversible-defect rows. Sensitivity: oldpeak 0.55, veto 2961 0.43, slope:3 0.33, slope:2 0.24, fbs:0 0.19, thal:7 0.19, restecg:2 0.02. Without the veto 557 would be on in 98 rows. Directly read out +1.470 (contribution SD 1.75) and also feeds 1239/9147. Mean-ablating 557 (all downstream): AUC 0.9589 -> 0.9236, the largest single drop.

parts.name: risk_factor_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Serial composition on top of the ischaemia gate: 9147 = ReLU(-1.522 + 1.027*557) is a second hinge that fires only for strong ischaemia (557 > 1.48); 1239 = ReLU(-0.457 + 0.933 sex:0 + 0.652 fbs:1 + 0.615 exang:1 + 0.216*557 + 0.105*9147), read out +1.964. It is a soft count of risk factors (female sex, diabetes, exercise angina, ischaemia) that cancels most of the large protective direct female term and the direct protective diabetes term once a woman or diabetic also has angina or ischaemia. Evidence (train): Train n=242: 1239 on in 120/242 rows; contribution SD 1.50. confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

For a typical patient it acts on, it lowers the predicted risk of heart disease from about 91% without this part to about 66% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 14 of these 28 patients had heart disease.

Through this part, resting blood pressure only adds to the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 109 mm Hg (between 97 and 140 mm Hg for different patients) for patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan: for a typical such patient, going from 94 mm Hg to 164 mm Hg moves it from about 88% to about 98%; across patients the change happens in an uneven way (on the training data only).

The model has little data on some of these: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: a downsloping ST segment (rather than any other slope of the ST segment at peak exercise) lowers it; resting blood pressure depending on fasting blood sugar raises it in an uneven way (on the training data only).
